summary: English Wikipedia (article "Colonnette", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A colonnette is a small slender column, usually decorative, which may support an arch, beam or lintel.

label: Heater core
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Heater core", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A heater core is a heat exchanger mounted in the cabin of a vehicle designed to provide heat that uses the same operating principles and working fluid as an automotive radiator.

label: Turbine trip
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Turbine trip", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A turbine trip is the automatic safety shutdown of a power-generation turbine due to unexpected events.

label: Linear actuator
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Linear actuator", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A linear actuator is an actuator that creates linear motion (i.e., in a straight line), in contrast to the circular motion of a conventional electric motor.

label: Copper loss
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Copper loss", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Copper loss is the term often given to heat produced by electrical currents in the conductors of transformer windings, or other electrical devices.

label: Deal–Grove model
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Deal–Grove model", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: The Deal–Grove model mathematically describes the growth of an oxide layer on the surface of a material.

label: Aerostructure
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Aerostructure", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: An aerostructure is a component of an aircraft's airframe.

label: Downstream (manufacturing)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Downstream (manufacturing)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Downstream, in manufacturing, refers to processes which occur later on in a production sequence or production line.

label: Design of experiments
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Design of experiments", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: The design of experiments (DOE), also known as experimental design, refers to the construction of procedures that attempt to explain how changes in one aspect of a system will lead to changes in other aspects of a system.

label: Change management (engineering)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Change management (engineering)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: The change request management process in systems engineering is the process of requesting, determining attainability, planning, implementing, and evaluating of changes to a system.

label: Bridge scour
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bridge scour", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Bridge scour is the removal of sediment such as sand and gravel from around bridge abutments or piers.

label: Exercise machine
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Exercise machine", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: An exercise machine is any machine used for physical exercise.

label: CVCC
summary: English Wikipedia (article "CVCC", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: CVCC, or Compound Vortex Controlled Combustion (Japanese: 複合渦流調整燃焼方式, Hepburn: Fukugō Uzuryū Chōsei Nenshō Hōshiki), is an internal combustion engine technology developed and trademarked by the Honda Motor Company.

label: BigDog
summary: English Wikipedia (article "BigDog", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: BigDog is a dynamically stable quadruped military robot platform that was created in 2005 by Boston Dynamics with the Harvard University Concord Field Station.

label: Cold welding
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cold welding", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Cold welding or contact welding is a solid-state welding process in which joining takes place without fusion or heating at the interface of the two parts to be welded.

label: Drilling
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Drilling", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Drilling is a cutting process where a drill bit is spun to cut a hole of circular cross-section in solid materials.

label: Gear failure
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Gear failure", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Sources of gear failure are varied, and are often based on the rotational speed and the load applied to the gear.

label: Coilgun
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Coilgun", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A coilgun is a type of mass driver consisting of one or more coils used as electromagnets in the configuration of a linear motor that accelerate a ferromagnetic or conducting projectile to high velocity.

label: Diaphragm valve
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Diaphragm valve", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A diaphragm valve, or membrane valve, consists of a valve body with two or more ports, a flexible diaphragm, and a weir, saddle, or seat upon which the diaphragm closes the valve.

label: Helix angle
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Helix angle", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In mechanical engineering, a helix angle is the angle between any helix and an axial line on its right, circular cylinder or cone.

label: Bulldog clip
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bulldog clip", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A bulldog clip is a device for temporarily but firmly binding sheets of paper together.

label: Bill of quantities
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bill of quantities", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A bill of quantities is a document used in tendering in the construction industry in which materials, parts, and labor (and their costs) are itemized.

sources.title: English Wikipedia article: Bill of quantities

label: Jackshaft (locomotive)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Jackshaft (locomotive)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A jackshaft is an intermediate shaft used to transfer power from a powered shaft such as the output shaft of an engine or motor to driven shafts such as the drive axles of a locomotive.

label: Architectural engineering
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Architectural engineering", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Architectural engineering or architecture engineering, also known as building engineering, is a discipline that deals with the engineering and construction of buildings, such as environmental, structural, mechanical, electrical, computational, embeddable, and other research domains.

label: Beamline
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Beamline", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: In accelerator physics, a beamline refers to the trajectory of the beam of particles, including the overall construction of the path segment (guide tubes, diagnostic devices) along a specific path of an accelerator facility.

label: Computer-aided engineering
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Computer-aided engineering", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Computer-aided engineering (CAE) is the general usage of technology to aid in tasks related to engineering analysis.

label: Column
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Column", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A column/pillar in architecture and structural engineering is a structural element that transmits, through compression, the weight of the structure above to other structural elements below.

label: Jewel bearing
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Jewel bearing", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A jewel bearing is a plain bearing in which a metal spindle turns in a jewel-lined pivot hole.

label: Bridge strike
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Bridge strike", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: Bridge strike or tunnel strike (also known as bridge bashing) is a transport accident in which a vehicle collides with a bridge, overpass, or tunnel structure.

label: Castellated beam
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Castellated beam", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A castellated beam is a beam style where an I-beam is subjected to a longitudinal cut along its web following a specific pattern.

label: Air data inertial reference unit
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Air data inertial reference unit", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: An air data inertial reference unit (ADIRU) is a key component of the integrated air data inertial reference system (ADIRS), which supplies air data (airspeed, angle of attack and altitude) and inertial reference (position and attitude) information to the pilots' electronic flight instrument system displays as well as other systems on the aircraft such as the engines, autopilot, aircraft flight control system and landing gear systems.

label: Change request
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Change request", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A change request, sometimes called change control request (CCR), is a document containing a call for an adjustment of a system; it is of great importance in the change management process.

label: Cable fairing
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Cable fairing", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A cable fairing is a structure attached to a towed cable designed to streamline the flow around the cable, primarily in marine environments.

label: Differential (mechanical device)
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Differential (mechanical device)", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A differential is a gear train with three drive shafts that has the property that the rotational speed of one shaft is the average of the speeds of the others.

label: Four-slide
summary: English Wikipedia (article "Four-slide", CC BY-SA 4.0) states: A four-slide, also known as a multislide, multi-slide, or four-way, is a metalworking machine tool used in the high-volume manufacture of small stamped components from bar or wire stock.
